Subject: Next steps: WellnessCo long-context pilot & model recommendations

Hi Anna — great to meet you and Devon on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short pilot testing actual notes ingestion and summarization fidelity.

Recap (call highlights):
- Primary goal: reliable end-to-end summarization of multi-hour therapy notes and care plans (many docs > 50k words) while preserving clinician extractables (meds, timestamps, tasks).
- Success metric: per-note key-fact recall >= 95% on our targeted prompt set and no regression in hallucination rate vs current baseline.
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive data (must be VPC & customer-managed keys for pilot), target latency for on-demand summary < 2s per 1k tokens after warm cache, and budget guardrails.

Model/architecture recommendations (first-pass):
1) Redwood-Instruct-13B-q4 (recommended) — strong cost/latency balance with long-context optimizations enabled (32k window profile).
2) Llama2-70b-chat (quantized variant) — higher-quality summaries on very long docs; higher cost, recommend for a small subset of critical notes.
3) Mistral-instruct-34B (eval-only) — good hallucination control on instruction prompts; include as comparison.

What we’re including in the pilot package:
- Evaluation harness (attached): ingestion scripts, sample prompt sets, automated metric scripts (ROUGE/F1/key-fact recall), and a small synthetic PHI-scrubbed dataset from our sandbox.
- Prompt bank: 10++ prompt variants for extractive + abstractive summarization and a canonical post-process checker to flag hallucinations. See long_context_prompt_sets.md.
- Benchmark snapshot: sample expected outputs and baseline metrics (attached CSV).

Known risk / truncation behavior notes:
- For contiguous notes > model context, our approach is to run a sliding-window semantic chunking with overlapping KV cache preservation and a final synthesis pass. This reduces truncation regressions but requires 2–3x token processing. We flagged areas where late-session context (notes appended after initial visit) produced missing timeline items in our internal tests.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm data residency & KMS requirements (you mentioned HSM support—please confirm).
2) We’ll spin up a 2-week Dedicated pilot (customer VPC) with 2 model variants + harness.
3) Internal kickoff: technical deep-dive with Marissa & Neha to finalize ingestion format and metric thresholds (30–45 minutes).
4) We’ll deliver a benchmark run within 72 hours of pilot data ingestion.

Options for a technical kick-off: Tue 2/16 10:00am PT or Wed 2/17 9:00am PT — which works for you?

Sending the attached eval harness and prompt sets now. If you want a lighter initial experiment, we can do a synthetic-only run that avoids PHI until legal signs off.

Thanks — Hannah

On Mon, Feb 15, 2027 at 09:08 AM Anna Li <anna@wellnessco.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Hannah — appreciate the fast follow-up and the materials. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock in dates:
> 1) Truncation specifics: you mentioned sliding-window + KV cache preservation. In practice, will the model be able to reference content that appears at the very start of a 100k-word record when producing a final timeline? We need a guarantee or mitigation (e.g., pinned prefixes).

Hi Anna — quick technical follow-up. Short answer: most models cannot natively attend to a 100k-token contiguous history in a single forward pass, but we have production patterns to approximate "global" context: 

- Pinned prefixes: yes — we can pin a canonical summary/metadata prefix (patient header with key identifiers, recent critical events) that is prepended to every chunk so the model always has that anchor. This is low-cost and highly effective for timeline integrity.

- Overlapping chunking + KV cache stitching: for models with KV cache support (Redwood-Instruct, Llama-family variants), we keep an incremental representation of intermediate summaries and stitch them in a final synthesis pass. This reduces missing-start issues but adds token work.

- Retrieval-augmented checks: we also run a verification pass against a lightweight vector index for sparse facts (med changes, dates). If the synthesis step produces a fact not present in the index, it’s flagged for human review.

Operational tradeoffs: 
- Cost: expect 2–3x token volume for sliding-window + synthesis compared to naive single-pass truncation.
- Latency: synthesis (final pass) adds ~200–800ms depending on chunking config; we can tune to meet your <2s per 1k token target by reducing overlap or using a smaller synthesis model.
- Guarantees: we can provide an SLA-backed fallback policy (e.g., fall back to a smaller extractive summary plus a human-in-loop review) for high-risk patients during the pilot.

PHI & KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys and detailed audit logs; HSM-backed KMS requires our Private deployment (VPC + HSM integration). For the pilot we can do a Dedicated pilot with strict audit logging, and then migrate to Private if you need FIPS/HSM. I’ll loop in our security lead if you want a formal architecture diagram.

Prompt & hallucination rubric (example):
- Extraction prompt (medication timeline):
  "You are a clinical summarization assistant. Extract medication changes from the note as bullets: date, medication name, dose (if present), change type (start/stop/adjust), clinician name. If unsure, return 'UNKNOWN' for that field and include the source sentence."

- Hallucination detection: automated checker will mark outputs where
  a) factual claim does not match any sentence in the source chunks (exact or fuzzy match), or
  b) a new medication name appears that has <0.2 fuzzy similarity to any token sequence in the indexed notes.

I’ll attach a short example of the prompt bank and a small sample output in the Drive folder we shared.

See you Wed 2/17 9:00am PT.

—Marissa
